newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SENATORS REWARD TUGNUTT WITH MULTI-YEAR CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SENATORS REWARD TUGNUTT WITH MULTI-YEAR CONTRACT.

text.p: Ron Tugnutt, the longtime backup goaltender who carried the Ottawa Senators to their first playoff berth this season, was rewarded by the team Friday with a multi-year contract.
Tugnutt took over for the injured Damian Rhodes as Ottawa's starting goalie late in the season and backstopped the club through the first successful drive for a playoff berth in franchise history.

He started the final 12 games of the season and went 9-1-2 with a 2.15 goals-against average and three shutouts as the Senators earned the seventh seed in the Eastern Conference after finishing dead last in the league their first four years in the NHL.

Tugnutt then turned in a stellar performance in the opening round of the playoffs as the Senators took the best-of-seven series to overtime in the seventh game before falling to the heavily-favoured Buffalo Sabres.

"Ron proved this season that he can be very successful in the NHL and his contribution to our playoff drive, in the final games of the season, and our strong playoff showing did not go unnoticed," Senators general manager Pierre Gauthier said in announcing the contract extension.
Tugnutt played all but four minutes in the seven-game playoff series, going 3-4 with a 1.98 goals-against average and a .917 save percentage.
"We are extremely pleased that Ron has decided to stay long-term with the Senators," said Gauthier, who did not release the terms of the new contract.
Rhodes, acquired from the New York Islanders late in the 1995-96 season, went 14-20-14 before a calf injury stopped him on March 22.
